title: Taylor Swift and Kelce Put NYC's Ambassadors Clubhouse and Indian Fine Dining in the Spotlight
excerpt: The newlyweds chose a high-end Punjabi restaurant in Manhattan's NoMad district for their first post-wedding NYC date night, highlighting the growing stature of Indian cuisine in America's dining capital.
body:
• Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce dined at Ambassadors Clubhouse, a high-end Punjabi restaurant in Manhattan's NoMad district, on September 6
  • The restaurant is run by JKS Restaurants, the group behind Michelin-starred Gymkhana, and features NYC's only coal-burning tandoor
  • Kelce has previously said Swift introduced him to Indian cuisine, and the couple dined at Gymkhana in London earlier this year
  • The outing reflects a growing wave of upscale Indian restaurants gaining mainstream celebrity attention in New York City

When Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce stepped out for their first New York City date night since their July wedding, they chose neither a French bistro nor a steakhouse. They went for Indian food.

The newlyweds were photographed on September 6 arriving at Ambassadors Clubhouse, a Punjabi fine-dining restaurant in Manhattan's NoMad neighborhood, according to People. Accompanied by two friends, the couple dined in the lower-ground main dining room, ordering what a source described as "a variety of classics from the menu."

A London Import With NYC Ambitions

Ambassadors Clubhouse, located at 1245 Broadway, is the first American outpost of the London restaurant of the same name. It opened in February 2025 and is operated by JKS Restaurants, the hospitality group founded by siblings Jyotin, Karam, and Sunaina Sethi — the same family behind Michelin-starred Gymkhana and more than 20 other venues across the UK.

The kitchen is led by Chef Karan Mittal, whose résumé includes a stint at the acclaimed Indian Accent. The menu draws from Northern India's culinary spectrum, from roadside chaat stalls to royal Punjabi feasts. Signature dishes include the Original BBQ Butter Chicken Chops — chicken charred in the restaurant's coal-burning tandoor and dressed in cashew and ghee masala — seven-layered samosas, and a masaledar lamb biryani with braised lamb shank and saffron.

"Ambassadors Clubhouse is a celebration of Northern India's vibrant culinary and hospitality traditions. Bringing the London restaurant to Manhattan allowed us to reimagine classic flavors in a way that is bold, playful, and entirely unique to this city."

— Karam Sethi, JKS Restaurants Co-Founder

The tandoor itself is a point of distinction: it burns coal rather than gas, making it the only one of its kind in New York City, according to the restaurant. The cocktail program follows the same ethos, weaving regional spices into classic recipes. The Patiala Peg — a Scotch old fashioned with Afghani saffron bitters, served tableside from a five-liter Johnnie Walker bottle — has become a signature pour.

Indian Cuisine in the Celebrity Mainstream

Swift and Kelce's visit is not their first Indian dining outing. In May, the couple ate at Gymkhana in London — another JKS property — where Kelce described the food as one of his "more surprising dining experiences." The tight end has previously credited Swift with introducing him to Indian cuisine.

The couple's September 6 outing came two months after their star-studded wedding at Madison Square Garden on July 3, which drew roughly 1,000 guests including Jennifer Lopez, Jessica Alba, and Ciara. Swift wore a metallic Stella McCartney halter dress for the dinner, while Kelce opted for an Amiri silk button-up with brown trousers.

The restaurant's two-floor space — designed with deep navy walls, rich textiles, and artwork by emerging British and American Punjabi artists — is styled after an Indian party palace. The Infatuation described it as "a capital R restaurant with undeniable charisma," noting its operatic scale and exaggerated Punjabi flavors.

A Broader Wave of Indian Dining in New York

Ambassadors Clubhouse's celebrity moment arrives during a broader shift in New York's dining landscape. London-born Indian restaurants are increasingly crossing the Atlantic: Bombay-inspired Dishoom, which draws queues at its Soho flagship in London, is slated for a permanent NYC location, and southern Indian-focused Kricket hosted a pop-up at Comal last year.

For the Indian diaspora, the trend represents more than a culinary novelty. Restaurants like Ambassadors Clubhouse are redefining how Punjabi food is perceived in the American mainstream — moving it from the neighborhood curry house to the same tier as French and Japanese fine dining. When the world's most photographed couple chooses an Indian restaurant for their most visible post-wedding outing, that shift becomes difficult to ignore.

What to Know Before You Go

Ambassadors Clubhouse is open daily for dinner from 5 p.m. to 11 p.m., with weekend brunch from noon to 3 p.m. Reservations are recommended — even the bar is a tough table to secure. Expect mains in the $32–$60 range. The restaurant seats guests across two floors, with a street-level parlor and a subterranean dining room where the couple was spotted.
nri_angle: Upscale Indian restaurants are breaking into the American celebrity mainstream, redefining how Punjabi cuisine is perceived in NYC fine-dining.
